newsitem.title: EGYPT: MIBANK in five-for-one share split.
newsitem.headline: MIBANK in five-for-one share split.

text.p: Shareholders in Egypt's Misr International Bank/MIBANK have approved a five-for-one share split to increase the stock's liquidity, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.

The bank has a total 4.5 million shares, some denominated in Egyptian pounds and others in dollars. At 750 pounds a share, the stock is bulky and the official told Reuters the split would further stimulate trading.
"We have not yet set a date for the split but it has been approved and will happen shortly," the official said.

He said the share split was in line with a shake-up of the bank's activity. MIBANK is also planning to increase its capital and is vetting 10 global securities houses before offering its shares through a global depositary receipt.
Last June the bank's board approved a bonus share for every two held. Trading in the stock has since helped fuel the recent record highs on the Egyptian stock exchange.

State-run Banque Misr holds 44.8 percent of MIBANK and Misr Insurance four percent. Banca di Roma has 10 percent, Luxembourg-based Europartners Holdings 7.9, Sakura Bank Ltd of Japan 2.6 and British Arab Commercial Bank 8.5 percent. Individuals own the remaining 22.2 percent.
